chapter: Later Blue Note years and ending the habit
title: Space and color from vibes and open accompanists
summary: Hutcherson, LaMont Johnson and Herbie Nichols gave McLean space and color unlike straight-ahead Cedar Walton.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What did that allow for you, musically?
Space and color. Because Bobby played a lot of colors, rainbows and things in his accompaniment.
Was he one of your favorite accompanists?

Oh yeah, definitely so. We’ve done a lot of duo things together and played a lot of things together that we can move from one concept to another, play standards, play this, play that. Bobby’s open for everything, like me.
Later on you compare LaMont Johnson to him, what he provided.
Yeah, right. LaMont was also very open to space and color.
What other accompanists have had that, have brought that to your . . . ?

Herbie Nichols, definitely. He was one of the first ones that I heard that brought that kind of feel. But there are a lot of piano players that are around that bring different things. Cedar is a highly competent accompanist, incredibly talented at that.
But not in such an open way. More of a . . .
